  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantifies the predictive value of animal tests for human drug toxicity using Likelihood Ratios (LRs), which is a measure of agreement between animal results and human clinical outcomes. It analyzes multiple species pairs and provides quantitative metrics for concordance (or lack thereof).",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study's primary focus is on predicting human drug toxicity and safety via animal tests, analyzing organ toxicity and adverse drug reactions.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study analyzes drug toxicity across various species and does not focus on a specific therapeutic area, making it cross-cutting.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes multiple species pairs including non-human primates, dogs, mice, rabbits, and rats, comparing their predictive value for human toxicity.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "rabbit",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly mentions analyzing data from 'non-human primates (NHPs) — arguably the most likely non-human species to have significant human relevance — asking the same question. In addition, we have examined the relationships of data from other pairs of these five non-human species, to assess how reliably tests in one species can indicate the toxicological susceptibility of any other species to new drugs. Our results for species including humans, NHPs, dogs, mice, rabbits, and rats...'",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses Likelihood Ratios (LRs) which incorporate both sensitivity and specificity to assess the predictive value of animal tests for human toxicity, encompassing both the presence and absence of toxicity."
